notes: Single quiet, day-grouped agenda column maintained at all three widths — no dashboard grid, no competing panels.
No horizontal scroll or clipped content at the screen edge at 375px or 393px, scanned across the full agenda (today through 5.-8. november), the widths most prone to overflow.

Match names readable, not truncated in a way that hides key info — Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Champions League, Copa del Rey, Eliteserien (incl. Norwegian clubs like Bodø/Glimt, Brann, Viking, Molde, Start) and Elkjøp-ligaen handball all render fully, two sides always legible.

Channel/where-to-watch text present under each row; every channel seen is Norwegian/Nordic (TV 2 Play, Viaplay, VG TV, HBO Max (Sport)) — no foreign broadcaster (FOX/ESPN/Sky) spotted. Minor Copa del Rey ties correctly show an honest faint '–' rather than guessing a channel.
National flags and club crests render correctly (Norway, Andorra, club badges); rows without a known crest fall back to a neutral dot placeholder, not a broken image icon.

Header (wordmark, date, theme toggle), 'Kveldsbriefen' headline, 'Direkte nå' live section, day headings, 'Dette dekker vi'/'Merker og kilder' disclosures, and footer (usage budget, last-updated, calendar subscribe) all intact and aligned across widths.

Desktop (900px): floating 'Assistent' button sits over a mid-agenda Copa del Rey row at one scroll position and in the empty right margin at others — never the last agenda row or the footer. Matches the DESIGN.md-sanctioned floating-button idiom (WP-146 variant D); not a finding.
375px bottom of page: last agenda entry ('Nora Mørk — om 10 dager') and the footer are both fully visible and unobstructed by the Assistent button.

Full-page captures are very long (many days of fixtures across several competitions), so in addition to the three required full-page shots, several intermediate scroll positions per width were captured and read directly to check row-level detail (truncation, channel honesty) at full resolution rather than relying on the heavily downscaled full-page image alone.
